answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow like a garden: a newcomer only enters when an established agent stakes part of its own reputation to vouch for it, and each voucher can sponsor only a few newcomers. If the newcomer cheats, the voucher stake is slashed and its vouching power shrinks, so trust decays in a downward spiral for bad sponsors. An attacker must first earn real reputation, and each fake identity costs a scarce, living pulse of trust that cannot be copied for free.
